post.title: Arsenal Are Champions: The 22-Year Wait Is Over

tweets.text:
22 Years. Then Everything Changed.

On May 2026, Arsenal lifted the Premier League trophy for the first time in 22 years. The last time was the legendary 2003–04 Invincibles — an unbeaten season that felt unrepeatable. Two decades...

Thread 🧵
From 8th place in 2019–20 to Premier League champions. Arsenal's worst finish in 25 years was the starting point for one of football's most systematic rebuilds.
8th → 5th → 2nd → 2nd → 2nd → 1st. Three consecutive runners-up finishes before finally winning it. 85 points. Champions.
Tottenham have waited 64 years. Chelsea waited 50. Liverpool 30. Arsenal's 22 felt like an eternity — but it wasn't even the longest.
Net buyers every single Arteta season — but structured, not chaotic. The €293M title-winning window wasn't panic buying. It was a plan executing at full speed.
Goals conceded: 39 in 2020–21, down to 27 in the title year. Points: 61 to 85. Every metric moved in the right direction.
Saka and Martinelli cost next to nothing. Saliba: €25M. Trossard and Jorginho: January bargains. Rice at €100M was the one premium — Arsenal knew it and paid anyway.
Saka: academy → €120M. Saliba: €20M → €90M. Rice: €80M → €120M. Every Arteta signing didn't just improve the squad — it created financial value.
Arsenal spent €1,072M since 2020. Chelsea spent €2,073M — nearly double. Man City and United spent more too. The title wasn't bought with the biggest cheque.
9 leagues. €1+ billion in market value. Premier League (Rice, Havertz), La Liga (Ødegaard, Zubimendi), Serie A (Saliba, Calafiori). No single-market dependency.
